summary: This bill amends the Child Nutrition Act of 1966 and the Richard B. Russell National School Lunch Act to make school breakfasts and lunches free for all children, eliminate meal debt collection by schools, and establish a program to reimburse schools for existing meal debt.

scores.thoughts: This bill significantly expands federal funding for school breakfast and lunch programs by making them free for all children, increasing reimbursement rates, and introducing new payments for locally sourced products. This will lead to a substantial increase in government expenditure.

The bill expands the social safety net by making school breakfast and lunch programs universally free for all children, removing eligibility requirements based on income, and prohibiting meal debt collection and 'lunch shaming.' This broadens access to nutritional support for all students, regardless of their family's economic status.

The bill's core purpose is to expand the school breakfast and lunch programs to provide free meals to every child, which requires substantially higher federal reimbursements to schools plus retroactive debt relief. No offsetting revenue or spending cuts are included, so the legislation directly increases mandatory spending and therefore pushes the budget toward a larger deficit.
